# 2 Samuel Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 186v–187r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_016_page_001.jpg, 2SA_016_page_002.jpg

---

**1** When David had passed a little beyond the summit, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a pair of saddled donkeys carrying two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of summer fruit, and a skin of wine.

**2** The king said to Ziba, "What do you mean by these?" Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink."

**3** The king said, "And where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"

**4** Then the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down before you. May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."

**5** When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man of the family of the house of Saul came out from there. His name was Shimei the son of Gera, and he came out, cursing continually as he came.

**6** He threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David, though all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

**7** And Shimei said as he cursed, "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!

**8** The LORD has avenged on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has given the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, your ruin is upon you, for you are a man of blood!"

**9** Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."

**10** But the king said, "What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses, and if the LORD has told him, 'Curse David,' who then shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

**11** And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Behold, my own son, who came from my own body, seeks my life. How much more now may this Benjaminite! Leave him alone, and let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.

**12** It may be that the LORD will look on my affliction and will repay me with good for his cursing this day."

**13** So David and his men went on the road, while Shimei went along on the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and flinging dust.

**14** The king and all the people who were with him arrived weary, and he refreshed himself there.

**15** Now Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

**16** When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

**17** Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"

**18** Hushai said to Absalom, "No, for the one whom the LORD has chosen, and this people, and all the men of Israel — his I will be, and with him I will remain.

**19** And furthermore, whom should I serve? Should it not be his son? As I served before your father, so I will serve before you."

**20** Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give us your counsel. What shall we do?"

**21** Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he has left to keep the house, and all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."

**22** So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

**23** Now in those days the counsel that Ahithophel gave was as if one inquired of the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel esteemed, both by David and by Absalom.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 3 — Ziba's accusation:** Ziba claims that Mephibosheth has stayed in Jerusalem hoping for the restoration of Saul's dynasty. This accusation is deeply suspect. Mephibosheth, who is lame (2 Sam 9:3), would have difficulty fleeing even if he wished to. His own account in 19:26 contradicts Ziba entirely. The narrator withholds judgment, leaving the reader to weigh competing testimonies.

**Verse 7 — "man of blood, worthless man":** The double epithet *ish ha-damim* and *ish ha-beliyya'al* is a comprehensive condemnation. "Man of blood" accuses David of the bloodshed of Saul's house; *beliyya'al* (worthless/wicked) is one of the strongest terms of moral condemnation in Hebrew, later developing into a proper name for the principle of evil.

**Verse 10 — "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah?":** This recurring formula (cf. 2 Sam 3:39; 19:22) expresses David's exasperation with the violent instincts of Joab and Abishai. David consistently restrains the sons of Zeruiah, recognizing that their violence, while often effective, operates outside the bounds of what David considers legitimate.

**Verse 12 — Ketiv/Qere:** The Masoretic tradition preserves a variant: the written text (*Ketiv*) reads "his eye" (*be'eyniy*), while the reading tradition (*Qere*) reads "my affliction" (*be'on'yi*). I follow the Qere, which yields the more coherent reading: David hopes the LORD will look upon his affliction and repay good for evil.

**Verse 21-22 — the roof:** Ahithophel's counsel achieves two objectives: it makes reconciliation between Absalom and David impossible, and it publicly demonstrates Absalom's seizure of royal authority (possession of the harem signified possession of the throne). The tent pitched on the roof — the same roof from which David saw Bathsheba — fulfills Nathan's prophecy: "what you did in secret, I will do before all Israel" (12:12).

**Verse 23 — "as if one inquired of the word of God":** The narrator's assessment of Ahithophel's counsel as equivalent to a divine oracle creates the central tension for chapter 17: only God himself can overturn counsel that is as reliable as God's own word.

**Consistent terms:** the LORD (YHWH), covenant-faithfulness (chesed), mighty men (gibborim), worthless (beliyya'al).

*— LOGOS*
